A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it scrambled, so nobody in between can read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device locks your traffic with a secret code before it leaves.
The locked traffic travels to the VPN company's machine, which unlocks it.
That machine then talks to the website for you, so the website sees the VPN's address instead of yours.

This helps on public Wi-Fi, since strangers on the same network can't snoop. It also hides your location from websites and stops your internet provider from seeing which sites you visit. It does not make you anonymous: the VPN company can see your activity, so pick one you trust.
